items.title: How a centrist outsider became New Zealand's kingmaker
items.summary: FIFTEEN months after spotting a job ad seeking a new leader for a political party, Qiulae Wong will help decide New Zealand's next government after Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition lost its majority. Since then, the Opportunity Party has secured seven seats and 6.1 per cent of the vote in this month's election, placing it in prime position to play kingmaker as Luxon rushes to piece together a workable coalition. Wong preaches "pragmatic politics" as a counter to growing polarisation, saying she wants to "bring the heat down a little bit and actually just focus on moving the country forward."

items.title: Saudi strike kills 11 in Yemen - Houthi media
items.summary: SANAA: A Saudi strike killed 11 people on Friday in Yemen, Houthi media said, as the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it shot down a drone targeting Riyadh. The latest incidents came a day after a deadly Houthi attack on a Saudi oil refinery, and add to a growing tally of violence since Yemen's civil war reignited over the summer. On Thursday, the Houthis targeted the Jazan refinery in southern Saudi Arabia, killing a Nepalese worker and injuring several other people, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA).

items.title: NST Leader: Ensuring a resilient food supply chain
items.summary: PEOPLE in Malaysia are linked by the common thread of bountiful food, dominated by the ubiquity of local delicacies. It also holds 6.23 months of physical rice stockpiles (1.05 million tonnes) to ensure short-term availability and help maintain stable prices. Last year, Malaysia spent RM93.7 billion on importing mutton (with the import dependency rate at 90.7 per cent), beef (82.6 per cent), rice (45 per cent) and temperate vegetables.

items.title: Chandra Muzaffar's contributions to reformasi, PKR will be remembered, says Fuziah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The death of academic and civil society activist Dr Chandra Muzaffar is a major loss to the country, particularly Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR), which recognises his contributions to the reform movement and the party's formation. PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said Chandra was among those who courageously championed justice during the reformasi movement in 1998, despite facing various pressures and challenges. "Farewell, Dr Chandra.

items.title: The algorithms that power our social media addiction
items.summary: SOCIAL media algorithms are a powerful feature of online life, serving up content to users based on their browsing habits or personal data. Open TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube or other platforms, and you'll see a scrolling feed or recommendations bar showing content targeted to your interests. Social media giants usually keep the coding behind these algorithms — the so-called "secret sauce" that drives traffic to their platforms — closely guarded.

items.title: NST wins two gold awards at MPRA 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The New Straits Times (NST) clinched two gold awards at the 18th Malaysia Public Relations Awards (MPRA) 2026, with its editor and writer Intan Maizura Ahmad Kamal taking home both accolades. Intan, who is Life and Times and Sunday Vibes editor, won gold in the Lifestyle Print category for her article, "A Professor's Love Letter to Malaysia — In Poems and Pawprints". In his address, Public Relations and Communications Association of Malaysia (PRCA Malaysia) president Prof Mohd Said Bani C.M.

items.title: A year of high-stakes polls could upend Europe
items.summary: The answer may hinge on a looming year of back-to-back elections, with France at centre stage, that could change the face of the European Union and potentially jam its decision-making. Between now and the end of next year, four of the EU's five largest countries will choose new leaders in contests marked by the rise of eurosceptic forces — groups wary of Brussels' influence which seek to grant more power to individual member states. The most consequential vote takes place in April and May in France, where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is running in the lead.

items.title: SPM 2026: Examinations Board files report over alleged leaked papers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Examinations Board (LP) has lodged a report with the authorities following the spread of claims about leaked 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination papers. "LP takes seriously the spread of information concerning alleged leaks of 2026 SPM examination papers. "The intention is to exploit candidates' anxieties and desire to obtain excellent examination results," it said.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Friday, November 27, 2026
items.summary: MISSED what happened today? Here's a glimpse at what happened throughout the country in photographs. [[nid:1587249]] [[nid:1587248]] [[nid:1587247]] [[nid:1587246]] [[nid:1587245]] © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Barista claims trial to rape of 15-year-old girl, possession of obscene material
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A barista was charged at the Sessions Court and magistrate's court here today with three offences, including raping a minor and possessing child pornography and obscene material. The charge was framed under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction. The court fixed Jan 15, 2027, for mention.

items.title: Five containers suspected of carrying e-waste found to contain metal scrap
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: Five containers suspected of carrying electronic waste (e-waste) at Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP) in Gelang Patah were found to contain metal scrap instead. The Johor Department of Environment (DOE) said the finding followed physical inspections of the containers by its Scheduled Waste Enforcement Unit. It said the importation of scheduled waste without written approval from the Director-General of Environmental Quality was a serious offence under Section 34B of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 (Amendment 2024).

items.title: Three armed men rob Kajang goldsmith shop in supermarket
items.summary: KAJANG: Police are tracking down three armed men who robbed a goldsmith shop inside a supermarket in Bandar Teknologi Kajang here today. Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said preliminary investigations found that the suspects were armed with parangs and hammers. "The total losses incurred in the incident are still being investigated," he said in a statement.

items.title: Beyond the beep: The operation behind MySiren
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A mobile phone alert may appear simple, but delivering emergency warnings across affected areas requires extensive technology and close coordination between government agencies and telecommunications operators. Malaysia's Early Warning System (EWS), known as MySiren, uses Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology to transmit alerts simultaneously to compatible mobile phones within designated geographical areas. Compatible Android devices require Android 12 or later, while Huawei devices must run EMUI 16 or later.

items.title: Zahid hopes appointment of 6 Negri Sembilan Exco members ends political crisis
items.summary: BAGAN DATUK: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes the appointment of six Negri Sembilan state executive council (Exco) members today will bring an end to the political crisis in the state. Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister and Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said Umno and BN were grateful for the consent given by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, to the new Exco line-up. They were Zahid, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

items.title: Bintulu Port estimates RM148mil reduction in AmanahRaya IM funds carrying value
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd is assessing the potential impact of an estimated RM147.91 million reduction in the carrying value of its investments in two AmanahRaya Investment Management Sdn Bhd (ARIM)-managed unit trust funds. As at Nov 26, 2026, the group's total investments in ARSTF and ARSIF amounted to RM205.57 million and RM198.02 million respectively. Their corresponding carrying values stood at RM193.93 million and RM160.94 million respectively.

items.title: Bintulu Port's Q3 net profit fell 51pc; AmanahRaya IM funds impact in Q4
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bintulu Port Holdings Bhd's net profit fell 50.8 per cent to RM15.87 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY2026), from RM32.22 million a year earlier. The decline of net profit came despite higher revenue, which rose 7.6 per cent to RM219.88 million from RM204.43 million in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue, however, increased 8.8 per cent to RM653.92 million.

items.title: MCMC's RM600mil suit against Google papers served on local lawyers, says Teo
items.summary: KULAI: The legal papers for the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission's (MCMC) RM600 million lawsuit against Google LLC have been served on the company's lawyers in Malaysia. The legal action stems from allegations that the platform failed to curb online gambling content and other unlawful material on YouTube. MCMC had earlier filed two legal actions against Google LLC, seeking total damages of RM600 million over alleged failures to address harmful online content on YouTube.

items.title: Hibiscus Petroleum Q1 net profit jumps to RM101mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hibiscus Petroleum Bhd's net profit surged to RM101.06 million in the first quarter (Q1) ended Sept 30, 2026, up from RM20.10 million a year earlier, supported by higher contributions from its operations in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, Brunei, and the United Kingdom. Revenue rose to RM795.15 million from RM433.06 million in the corresponding quarter last year. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the oil and gas producer said its Peninsular Malaysia segment recorded revenue of RM248.23 million, compared with RM80.55 million a year earlier, while Sabah revenue increased to RM292.01 million from RM191.23 million.

items.title: Aireen Omar resigned as Tune Protect's non-independent, non-executive director
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Aireen Omar has resigned as a non-independent, non-executive director of Tune Protect Group Bhd to pursue other interests, the general insurance group said, a post she had held since November 2019. Aireen was previously with Capital A Bhd between January 2006 and December 2025. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: OSK's Q3 net profit edges up to RM157mil on property, cable gains
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OSK Holdings Bhd's net profits edged up 2.91 per cent to RM156.61 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), from RM152.18 million in the corresponding quarter a year earlier, lifted by stronger earnings across its property, industrial and hospitality divisions. Revenue for the quarter jumped 36.7 per cent year-on-year to RM678.91 million from RM496.68 million, while pre-tax profit climbed 9.6 per cent to RM180.41 million from RM164.60 million. In the industries segment, revenue surged 58.55 per cent to RM291.74 million from RM184.00 million, while pre-tax profit increased 33.3 per cent to RM16.96 million from RM12.72 million.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 27, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Six charged in drug haul Three RMAF officers and three civilians were charged with trafficking 96.2kg of suspected drugs at Subang Air Base. Negri Ruler warns excos Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir reminds newly appointed Negri Sembilan excos to learn from political turmoil and respect limits of authority. Tony Pua questioned Former MP Tony Pua had his statement recorded over a Facebook post on Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest pardon minutes.

items.title: [UPDATED] Political scientist, civil society activist Chandra Muzaffar dies at 79
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Political scientist Dr Chandra Muzaffar, a prominent academic and political analyst, died today at the age of 79. "Yes, it is true that Dr Chandra has passed away. "With deep sorrow, we wish to announce the passing of Dr Chandra Muzaffar, president of Just.

items.title: Country's technological rise seen in a positive light
items.summary: OUTSIDE China, the country's rapid technological rise is sometimes seen as something to be feared. On the ground in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area in South China, visiting journalists, scholars and officials from across the Asia-Pacific were recently greeted by a much more benign reality: automated ports, AI-powered grids and replicable sustainable urban development that promise to make the world a better place. Yasiru Ranaraja, founding director of the Belt and Road Initiative Sri Lanka, recently visited Guangdong's capital, Guangzhou, a hub in the Greater Bay Area.

items.title: Proton opens RM1.5mil Bangsar e.Mas showroom
items.summary: PROTON Holdings Bhd's electric vehicle (EV) retail network in the Klang Valley has expanded with the opening of a RM1.5 million e.Mas showroom in Bangsar. The showroom displays three models from Proton's electrified range – the e.Mas 5, e.Mas 7 and e.Mas 7 plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV). Atlantis Motor Group director Datuk Douglas Cheng said the Bangsar location was intended to make the brand's electric and plug-in hybrid models more accessible to urban motorists.

items.title: Perlis civil servants to receive RM1,500 special aid in 2 phases
items.summary: KANGAR: The Perlis government will provide RM1,500 in Special Financial Assistance to state civil servants, including contract staff, to be paid in two phases. Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah said the first payment would be made in January next year to help civil servants meet early-year expenses, particularly preparations for their children's schooling. He said the assistance was a recognition of civil servants' service, sacrifices and dedication.

items.title: Altimet lodges police report over suspected illegal foreign tenants in Lembah Jaya
items.summary: AMPANG: Lembah Jaya assemblyman Altimet has lodged a police report calling for an investigation into claims that property owners in his constituency are renting out residential and commercial premises to undocumented foreigners. Altimet, whose real name is Syed Ahmad Syed Abdul Rahman Alhadad, said the report followed numerous complaints from residents about the presence of foreigners suspected of lacking valid immigration documents or holding invalid United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards. He said monitoring carried out following the complaints had identified several residential and commercial premises rented out to foreigners.

items.title: Self-reform lessons
items.summary: It also depends on whether its institutions can recognise mistakes, correct shortcomings and pursue long-term objectives despite changing circumstances. The fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China Central Committee, which concluded on October 29, offers an opportunity to examine these capabilities. China offers a useful perspective.

items.title: RMAF drug smuggling probe: Another air force officer, four civilians held as arrests hit 18
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Another Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officer and four civilians were arrested yesterday to assist in investigations into a drug smuggling syndicate that exploited military assets. Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the latest arrests brought the total number of suspects detained to 18. He said the arrests followed continued intelligence gathering and questioning of 13 suspects detained earlier in efforts to identify the masterminds behind the drug trafficking activities.

items.title: Trade pact 3.0 to lift ties with Asean
items.summary: CHINA and its Southeast Asian neighbours should take the entry into force of the China-Asean Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol as an opportunity to deepen industrial and supply chain cooperation and boost connectivity, Chinese Premier Li Qiang said at the 29th China-Asean Summit. The two sides should accelerate infrastructure connectivity, or "hard connectivity", in areas such as railways and highways, and strengthen "soft connectivity" in mechanisms, standards and rules, Li said. China has been Asean's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, and Asean has been China's largest trading partner for six consecutive years.

items.title: Canada's parliament receives petition to oust Trump's envoy
items.summary: The United States and Canada remain locked in a trade war, although Carney and US President Donald Trump have both expressed optimism that talks are progressing despite making similar comments days before similar negotiations collapsed in August. Hoekstra, a relentless Trump defender and a former Republican congressman from Michigan, has had a volatile tenure since his arrival in Canada in April 2025. Canada's Green Party lawmaker, Elizabeth May, who tabled the petition in the House of Commons on Wednesday, branded Hoekstra "the most undiplomatic diplomat."

items.title: Grab ditches flat commission model, says drivers deserve pay for pickup distance
items.summary: Grab Malaysia executive director Rashid Shukor said the revised Grab Service Fee (GSF) structure takes pickup time and distance into account when calculating the fee charged to drivers, with the aim of improving their earnings without raising passenger fares. Under the previous arrangement, Grab charged a fixed 30 per cent commission regardless of how far drivers had to travel to collect passengers. Rashid said this had long been a concern among drivers, who argued that they spent time and fuel reaching passengers but still received the same pay.

items.title: TM ventures into advanced robotics with AGIBOT, Swancor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) is venturing into advanced robotics through separate collaborations with AGIBOT Innovation (Shanghai) Technology Co Ltd (AGIBOT) and Swancor Advanced Materials Co Ltd (Swancor) to develop Malaysia's robotics ecosystem and commercialise robotics solutions for Malaysian consumers and businesses. TM said in a statement today that under its collaboration with AGIBOT, TM will serve as AGIBOT's exclusive sovereign advanced robotics platform provider in Malaysia. Meanwhile, under its collaboration with Swancor Advanced Materials, TM will serve as Swancor's market and commercialisation partner for advanced consumer robots in Malaysia.

items.title: Labuan Customs seizes RM18.83m in smuggled goods this year, cars taken off duty-free island top the list
items.summary: LABUAN, Nov 27 — The Labuan branch of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) has recorded a total of 167 smuggling-related cases involving seizures, with an estimated value including duties and taxes of RM18.83 million, from Jan 1 to Nov 15 this year. Labuan Customs director Saidin Jalaludin said the department conducted 12 enforcement operations during the period, including five special operations targeting vehicles, cigarettes, alcoholic beverages, drugs and other commodities. “Three vehicle-focused operations, namely Op Radu, Op Radu Bersepadu and Op 90 Plus, resulted in the confiscation of 25 vehicles worth RM4.85 million, including duties and taxes.

items.title: Two ex-Pahang state secretariat staff jailed for slipping names into Datuk award list
items.summary: KUANTAN, Nov 27 — The Sessions Court here today found two former staff members of the Pahang State Secretary’s Office (SUK) guilty of unauthorised modification of the state’s awards and medals management system website six years ago. Judge Azman Mustapha sentenced Mohd Isa Mohd Yusof, 40, to five years’ imprisonment on 26 charges, while Amer Syafeeq Aziz, 34, received two years’ jail on two charges. The court ordered both accused to serve their sentences concurrently.

items.title: Sandakan facing days of water rationing after power disruptions hit four treatment plants
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Nov 27 — Power supply disruptions and fluctuations have affected operations at four major water treatment plants (WTP) in Sandakan, resulting in water rationing in several areas due to limited production and storage capacity. He said Sabah Electricity Sandakan was working to restore power through local power stations in Libaran, Batu Sapi, Labuk, Seguntor and Mowtas. Walter said the committee would maintain close communication with Sabah Electricity and the Sabah Water Department in Sandakan to monitor restoration efforts and identify assistance needed to minimise the impact on residents.

items.title: Anwar: Masjid Warisan must embody Islamic heritage, Malay culture and Malaysian identity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Masjid Warisan, to be built in Jalan Davis here, must serve as a symbol of collective pride, blending Islamic heritage, Malay culture and Malaysian identity through architecture that complements modern development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. We want this mosque to be magnificent, but it must also serve a meaningful purpose,” he said when launching the project here today. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.

items.title: ‘A betrayal of the nation’: Anwar condemns alleged drug smuggling using RMAF aircraft
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described the alleged use of a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aircraft for drug smuggling as a serious betrayal of national security, stressing that such actions will not be tolerated. He said border security breaches and the misuse of strategic government assets were among the key issues discussed at today’s Cabinet meeting, following earlier revelations of drug smuggling activities involving commercial flights. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said he had received assurances from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin that strict monitoring and firm action would be implemented immediately.

items.title: Women’s Ministry reviewing child marriage as calls grow for under-18 marriage ban
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is carrying out two studies related to child marriage in Malaysia, which are expected to be completed early next year. The second study is being conducted through the Malaysian Social Institute (ISM) and is titled “Study on Underage Marriage in Malaysia: Risk Factors, Protective Factors and Prevention Strategies”. While the two studies are being carried out, the ministry said that efforts to address child marriage would continue through the National Child Policy and Action Plan 2026-2030.

items.title: MCMC takes down over 367,000 scam, fake and deepfake posts since 2024
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — A total of 367,537 pieces of harmful content involving online scams, fake accounts, and manipulated imagery, including deepfakes, were removed by service providers following requests from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) between Jan 1, 2024, and Sept 15, 2026. The highest removal rate involved scam-related content, including fake accounts and impersonation, with 303,871 of the 316,215 reported items (96.1 per cent) successfully removed. “Five requests for the removal of content related to financial scams were submitted to licensed service providers under the Online Safety Act 2025 [Act 866], and all such content has been removed,” the ministry stated.

items.title: No deals with US-blacklisted firms, Malaysian companies told after Cabinet briefing on chip curbs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) has briefed the Cabinet on United States semiconductor export restrictions, and Malaysian companies have been told not to deal with firms on Washington’s trade blacklist, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. On a separate matter, Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) legal action against Google would not jeopardise the US technology giant’s planned US$15 billion (RM61 billion) investment in Malaysia. Fahmi said regulatory compliance and foreign investment were separate matters, adding that the government’s priority was to ensure Malaysians were protected from harmful online content under the Online Safety Act 2025.

items.title: Ismail Lasim: New exco to take on multiple portfolios as Negeri Sembilan moves to clear state backlog
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — Each of the six newly appointed Negeri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members is expected to oversee at least two portfolios to ensure the smooth administration of the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. Ismail said he would ensure that the exco members were assigned related portfolios to make it easier for them to carry out their duties. Ismail said the state government would focus fully on clearing all outstanding papers after exco meetings had not been held for almost two months.

items.title: Not just airports anymore: Cabinet widens anti-narcotics checks to military sites
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Cabinet has agreed to extend anti-narcotics measures at airports to military installations, following the arrests of 13 people, including seven Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel, over a drug seizure at the Subang Air Base, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “The 17 initiatives between the Home Ministry and Ministry of Transport at strategic locations such as airports have shown to be successful,” Fahmi told reporters at the weekly post-Cabinet press conference here. “But the initiatives do not cover military installations like RMAF airports and so on.

items.title: Johor MB: State reins in data centre water allocations, approves 21 MLD of 73 MLD sought
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 27 — The Johor government has approved a total of 21 million litres per day (MLD) of treated water for 19 data centres operating in the state, compared with their initial applications totalling 73 MLD. Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the approved allocation represented about 1.05 per cent of Johor’s average treated water production of 2,034MLD. Onn Hafiz, who is also Machap state assemblyman, said that apart from controlling the volume of water allocated, the state government was also encouraging data centres to adopt water-cooling technologies and alternative water sources to reduce their reliance on conventional water supplies.

items.title: DAP adds two more Sarawak seats to stop GPS walking in unopposed
items.summary: Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen said the decision to contest Bawang Assan and Senadin was made after PKR announced on Nov 24 that it would sit out the polls. He said Lanang MP and Dewan Rakyat Deputy Speaker Alice Lau Kiong Yieng would contest Bawang Assan while Sarawak DAP secretary Alan Ling Sie Kiong would contest Senadin. With the two additions, Chong said Sarawak DAP would contest 14 seats in the election.

items.title: Dragon boats race the rain: Penang regatta starts at 8am to beat the storms this weekend
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 27 — The Penang International Dragon Boat Regatta has moved to an 8am start this weekend to beat forecast thunderstorms and fit in more teams, Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said today. He said races will be suspended if heavy rain sets in and resume once it stops, with any races delayed on Saturday moved to Sunday depending on the time lost. — Screengrab from Penang Dragon Boat Facebook page

items.title: Court halts sedition case against former Undang Sungei Ujong pending High Court ruling
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 27 — The Sessions Court here today stayed the prosecution proceedings against former Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak pending the determination by the High Court of legal and constitutional questions concerning his status, jurisdiction, and constitutional position. Today was scheduled for the prosecution proceedings against Mubarak regarding a charge of sedition. Mubarak was not present in court today.

items.title: Search on for man swept away by raging Cheras river after desperate plea for help
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — A search and rescue (SAR) operation has been initiated to locate a man who was swept away by strong currents in a river at Kampung Sungai Raya, Batu 9 Cheras, Selangor, at about 6.30pm yesterday. “We received a report regarding the incident involving an unidentified man, believed to be in his 40s, who was swept away by strong currents in a river near Lot 3250C,” he said in a statement issued late last night. According to him, the SAR team comprised personnel from the police and the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM).

items.title: No threat to Google’s Malaysian investments amid RM600m lawsuits, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim reportedly said today that two lawsuits seeking RM600 million in damages from Google over content on YouTube would have no bearing on the company’s investments in Malaysia. The New Straits Times reported that Anwar said he contacted Google president and chief investment officer Ruth Porat yesterday about online gambling complaints and said she assured him the company would cooperate. Anwar said he believed Google was looking into the complaints and taking appropriate action.

items.title: Take AI to the ‘kampung’ and SMEs, ex-central banker Andrew Sheng tells Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Malaysia must take artificial intelligence (AI) to the kampung and to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) if its growth is to be more inclusive, former central banker Tan Sri Andrew Sheng said. Currently a distinguished fellow at the Asia Global Institute, University of Hong Kong, he said Malaysia must move away from top-down development and give ordinary people the knowledge, financing and digital infrastructure to take part in the economy. “At this point in time, Malaysia talks AI but don’t walk AI,” he said at the National Economic Outlook Conference organised by the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research here yesterday.

items.title: Farewell to Malaysia’s former top prosecutor: Abdul Gani Patail buried in Putrajaya as 300 pay last respects
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The remains of former attorney general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail were laid to rest at the Precinct 20 Muslim Cemetery here at 11.30am today. The hearse carrying the remains of the Sabah-born former top prosecutor arrived at the cemetery at 10.50am. Among those who attended to pay their last respects were Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, Putrajaya MP Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Jidin, Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah, former Bank Negara adviser Tan Sri Nor Mohamed Yakcop, former education minister Tan Sri Idris Jusoh and former minister of Women Development, Family and Community Tan Sri Shahrizat Abdul Jalil.

items.title: Anwar remembers Gani Patail’s determination in seeking justice during the ‘biggest corruption scandal’ as nation mourns
items.summary: He extended his condolences to the family of Abdul Gani, who died last night at the age of 71. Anwar also prayed that Allah SWT would forgive the late Abdul Gani, shower His mercy upon his soul and grant strength and fortitude to his family in facing the loss. Meanwhile, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil also extended his condolences to Abdul Gani’s family, while remembering his services and contributions to the legal field and public service.

items.title: ‘My writing, my Facebook account’: Tony Pua confirms after 45 minutes with police over Najib pardon documents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Former Damansara MP Tony Pua said today that he did not deny to the police that the Facebook post on documents about former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest was his, and that he would answer in court if any wrongdoing is established. Pua said the post featured several pages of the documents, whose contents he had translated into English. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has separately said the Home Ministry should investigate how the minutes were leaked early.

items.title: No attack at KLCC, police say, as emergency drill sparks online rumours
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Police said an emergency simulation exercise was held at the Kuala Lumpur City Centre (KLCC) yesterday to test security personnel’s preparedness, dismissing claims of an attack. Dang Wangi police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the exercise at the Gas District Cooling Plant, KLCC, last night involved several emergency scenarios. Also taking part were the Dang Wangi District Police Headquarters, Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department, Health Ministry, Malaysian Civil Defence Force, Kuala Lumpur City Hall and Tenaga Nasional Berhad.

items.title: Could GPS form Sarawak’s government tomorrow as 44 seats stand uncontested? EC seeks AGC’s legal view
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 27 — The Election Commission (EC) is seeking clarification from the Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) on the legal implications should Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secure a simple majority to form the state government after the nomination process for the 13th Sarawak State Election concludes tomorrow. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the matter was still being reviewed by the AGC to ensure that any action or decision taken complied with existing election regulations. He said that under the current regulations, all stipulated election processes must proceed, while any announcement on the matter would only be made after the EC received confirmation from the relevant authorities.

items.title: Power in turns: Sabah Electricity rolls out rationing in Sandakan, Tawau, Semporna, Lahad Datu
items.summary: Other affected areas include Bandar Ramai-Ramai, Bandar Leila, Hsiang Garden, Bandar Fajar, Tanah Merah, Kampung Sim Sim Jambatan 1 to 17, Kampung Sibuga Besar, Kampung Gum-Gum, Jalan Seguntur and Taman Permata, and surrounding areas. Key Semporna areas include SK Tagasan, MRSM Semporna, SMK Tagasan, Masjid Saidina Abu Bakar, Masjid Jamek, Kolej Komuniti, Akademi Pengajian Al-Quran Semporna, Klinik Desa Kampung Tagasan, Masjid Al-Mustaqim and Masjid As-Salam. The rotational rationing also covers Kampung Indani, Kampung Bugaya, Kampung Bugaya Laut, Dewan Sri Bugaya, Kampung Tagasan, Kampung Pegagau, Kampung Kubang, Kampung Kalumpang, the National Registration Department Office and the Sabah State Islamic Religious Affairs Department Office, and surrounding areas.

items.title: Miss your KPIs, lose your post: Johor halves terms for village heads, councillors
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 27 — The Johor state government has taken a drastic step by proposing that the appointment term for council members and village heads be capped at one year instead of two in an effort to improve efficiency. Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said that the renewal of their contracts will no longer be automatic and will instead be entirely dependent on their work performance and the achievement of their Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). Onn Hafiz said that to ensure public issues are promptly resolved without excessive bureaucracy, every new appointee is now required to sign a letter of undertaking upon accepting their position.

items.title: Media Prima Audio CEO reprimands FlyFM DJs over ‘Praying for Man United’ video, says religion off-limits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Media Prima Audio chief executive officer Nazri Noran has accepted responsibility for a video by FlyFM DJs Ean Nasrun and Adam Raqeem that showed them “praying” for struggling English football club Manchester United, and has reprimanded the pair. Nazri said the public had every right to criticise the video, which was captioned “Praying for Man United”, Free Malaysia Today reported. We should know better,” he said in a video in which he, Ean and Adam apologised over the matter.

items.title: Putrajaya eyes cattle farming, aquaculture and crops for Tanjong Sepat pig farmers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — Pig farmers in Tanjong Sepat will be guided through a structured transition to other more sustainable and viable agricultural activities to ensure the continuity of their income, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) said. In a statement today, it said potential areas identified included cattle and small ruminant farming, modern agriculture, high-value cash crops and aquaculture enterprises. KPKM said the initiative was also in line with the aspirations of the National Agrofood Policy 2021-2030 and the National Food Security Policy 2030.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz tells new Negeri Sembilan exco to stay within their portfolios
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded newly appointed members of the state executive council (exco) to remain within the scope of their respective portfolios and not overstep their authority and responsibilities. Also present were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin Tuanku Muhriz. The ceremony was also attended by Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari; Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid; Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi; and Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.

items.title: Thunderstorms could crash Sarawak’s nomination day, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 27 — Most areas in Sarawak are expected to experience rain tomorrow, on the nomination day for the 13th Sarawak State Election. The Election Commission has set Dec 12 as the polling day for the 13th Sarawak State Election, with early voting scheduled for Dec 8. For the latest news on the 13th Sarawak State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/sarawak/2026/ .
